source_text: Ἀνθρώπῳ δὲ ἀδύνατόν τι γνῶναι, καὶ παρὰ ἀνθρώπου μαθεῖν τὰ ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς, ἢ τὰ ἐπιόντα. Τίς γὰρ ἔσται ὁ μηνύσων; Ἄνθρωπος δὲ ὃς οὐκ οἶδεν εἰς τὴν ἀγαθὴν πορευθῆναι πόλιν, κάκωσιν ὑπομένει, τοῖς τε ὀφθαλμοῖς, καὶ τῷ παντὶ προσώπῳ. Πόλει δὲ ἐκείνῃ κακὰ προλέγω, ἧς ὅ τε βασιλεὺς νέος, καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες γαστρίμαργοι. Μακαρίζω δὲ γῆν τὴν ἀγαθὴν, ἧς βασιλεύει ὁ τοῦ ἐλευθέρου υἱός· ἔνθα εὐκαίρως ἀπολαύσουσιν ἀγαθῶν, οἱ ἐκεῖσε ἄρχειν ἠξιωμένοι. Ὀκνηρὸς δὲ καὶ ἀργὸς, οἶκον ἐλαττοῦσι χλευασταὶ γενόμενοι· καὶ εἰς τὴν ἑαυτῶν λαιμαργίαν, τοῖς πᾶσι καταχρώμενοι, ἀργυρίῳ ἀγώγιμοι, ἕνεκα ὀλίγου τιμήματος πάντα αἰσχρῶς καὶ ταπεινῶς πράσσειν ὑπομένοντες. Βασιλεῖ δὲ, καὶ ἄρχουσιν, ἢ δυνάσταις ὑπακούειν προσήκει, καὶ οὐκ ἀπεχθάνεσθαι, οὐδ᾽ ὅλως λυπηρόν τι εἰς αὐτοὺς ῥῆμα ἀποῤῥίπτειν. Δέος γὰρ, μὴ τὸ καὶ τὸ καταμόνας εἰρημένον, εἰς φανερόν πως ἔλθῃ. Τῷ γὰρ μόνῳ καὶ πλουσίῳ καὶ μεγάλῳ βασιλεῖ ἄγγελοι ὀξεῖς καὶ ὑπόπτεροι ἅπαντα διακομίζουσι, πνευματικὴν ὁμοῦ καὶ λογικὴν τελοῦντες ὑπηρεσίαν.
thought_title: Human inability to know and the contrast between good and bad rule
orientation: Solomon (reported) declares that humans cannot know past or future, laments a city under a young king and gluttonous rulers, praises a land ruled by a free man's son, condemns lazy officials who exploit everyone for money, and warns against cursing the powerful because angels serve the one great King.
pass_a_gloss: For a human being, it is impossible to know anything, and to learn from a human being the things from the beginning, or the things coming upon us. For who will be the one announcing? But a human being who does not know how to go to the good city suffers affliction, in the eyes and in the whole face. Moreover, I announce evils beforehand for that city, of which both the king is young, and the rulers are gluttonous. But I count blessed the good land, of which the son of the free man reigns; there those deemed worthy to rule there will enjoy good things seasonably. But the slothful and idle man, having become mockers, diminish a house; and for their own gluttony, using all people, led by silver, they endure to do all things shamefully and basely for a small price. But it is fitting to obey a king, and rulers, or potentates, and not to hate them, nor to cast away any grievous word at all against them. For fear, lest the thing said in private, somehow come into the open. For to the only and rich and great king, angels, sharp and winged, carry all things, performing spiritual and rational service together.

lemmas.gloss: the things coming upon us / the future things
to go to the good city
to cast away a word / reject a word

choices.english: For a human being it is impossible to know anything
choices.why: Dative of person with impersonal adjective; 'τι' = anything at all. The glossary has no entry for this phrase; literal rendering keeps the force of total inability.
rejected: It is impossible for a man to know something

choices.english: to go to the good city
choices.why: Purpose infinitive with motion verb; 'good city' contrasts with the city under a young king. No glossary entry; literal keeps spatial and moral sense.
rejected: to journey to the good city

choices.why: Compound γαστήρ + μαργαίνω; 'slaves to the belly' is the literal sense. Glossary has no entry; 'gluttonous' is the standard English equivalent without hyphenation.

choices.term: Ὀκνηρὸς δὲ καὶ ἀργὸς, οἶκον ἐλαττοῦσι χλευασταὶ γενόμενοι
choices.english: But the slothful and idle man, having become mockers, diminish a house
choices.why: Singular subject 'Ὀκνηρὸς ... ἀργὸς' with plural participle 'χλευασταὶ γενόμενοι' — the slothful man becomes a mocker (plural of class). 'ἐλαττοῦσι' = diminish / lessen. Kept literal.
rejected: the lazy and idle, becoming scoffers, lessen a household
slothful idlers, turned mockers, shrink a house

choices.why: Dative of agent/cause with adjective 'ἀγωγός' (leading, guiding). 'Money-driven' is interpretive; 'led by silver' preserves the spatial metaphor.

choices.term: Δέος γὰρ, μὴ τὸ καὶ τὸ καταμόνας εἰρημένον, εἰς φανερόν πως ἔλθῃ
choices.english: For fear, lest the thing said in private, somehow come into the open
choices.why: Δέος = fear (nominative of cause). 'τὸ καὶ τὸ' = the particular thing / this and that. 'καταμόνας' = alone, in private. 'πως' = somehow. Subjunctive 'ἔλθῃ' after μὴ = purpose/fear clause. Literal keeps the caution.
rejected: For fear that what was said in private might somehow become public
Because of fear, lest the private word come out

bible_refs.note: ὃς οὐκ οἶδεν εἰς τὴν ἀγαθὴν πορευθῆναι πόλιν — corresponds to 'who knows not how to go to the city' (Eccl 10:14 LXX).
ὅ τε βασιλεὺς νέος, καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες γαστρίμαργοι — corresponds to 'woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and thy princes eat in the morning' (Eccl 10:16 LXX).
Μακαρίζω δὲ γῆν τὴν ἀγαθήν, ἧς βασιλεύει ὁ τοῦ ἐλευθέρου υἱός — corresponds to 'blessed art thou, O land, when thy king is the son of nobles' (Eccl 10:17 LXX).
Ὀκνηρὸς δὲ καὶ ἀργὸς, οἶκον ἐλαττοῦσι χλευασταὶ γενόμενοι — corresponds to 'by slothfulness the building shall be brought low' (Eccl 10:18 LXX).
εἰς τὴν ἑαυτῶν λαιμαργίαν ... ἀργυρίῳ ἀγώγιμοι — corresponds to 'money answereth all things' (Eccl 10:19 LXX).

Βασιλεῖ δὲ ... οὐκ ἀπεχθάνεσθαι ... Δέος γὰρ, μὴ τὸ καὶ τὸ καταμόνας εἰρημένον, εἰς φανερόν πως ἔλθῃ — corresponds to 'curse not the king ... for a bird of the air shall carry the voice' (Eccl 10:20 LXX).

pass_b_english: It is impossible for a human being to know anything, and to learn from a human being the things from the beginning or the things that are coming. For who will be the one to declare them? A human being who does not know how to go to the good city endures affliction, in his very eyes and in his whole face. I declare evils for that city whose king is young and whose rulers are gluttonous. But I call blessed the good land whose king is the son of the free man; there those deemed worthy to rule will enjoy good things in due season. The slothful and idle man, having become a mocker, diminishes a house; and driven by his own gluttony, using everything for it, led by silver, he endures doing all things shamefully and basely for a trifling price. It is fitting to obey a king, and rulers, and potentates, and not to make oneself hateful to them, nor to cast away any troublesome word toward them at all. For fear, lest the thing said in private somehow come into the open. For to the one king, rich and great, sharp and winged angels carry all things, rendering a service both spiritual and rational.

problems.why: ἀπεχθάνεσθαι means to make oneself hated or to be hostile toward someone. It does not mean 'to hate'. The English gets the agency wrong.
problems.fix: and not to make oneself hateful to them
problems.ruling: ἀπεχθάνεσθαι with dative βασιλεῖ means become hateful to them; “hate them” reverses who bears the hostility.

edits.new: and not to make oneself hateful to them

fixed: and not to hate them -> source has καὶ οὐκ ἀπεχθάνεσθαι (middle voice: 'make oneself hated/become hateful to'), not active 'hate'; corrected agency

last_rejected.why: ἀργυρίῳ ἀγώγιμοι means buyable or liable to be carried off for silver, not that silver leads him.
last_rejected.fix: buyable for silver, he stoops to do everything shamefully and basely for a trifling price.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀγώγιμοι means 'leadable, pliable', and ἀργυρίῳ is a dative of means or price. 'Led by silver' is awkward but keeps the sense of being swayed by money.
